content: Wrapping 'use Ecto.Schema' or 'use Ecto.Migration' in Code.ensure_loaded?() does NOT work — the use macro expands at compile time before the condition is evaluated, causing CompileError if the dep is missing. The correct patterns: (1) Wrap the ENTIRE module definition in 'if Code.ensure_loaded?(Ecto) do ... end' — this works because module definitions are also macros. (2) Alternative: Mark ecto/ecto_sql as non-optional in mix.exs but with 'only: [:dev, :test]' if only used in dev/test, but this won't work for library users. (3) For library distribution, the Oban pattern: the library defines migration modules normally (requiring ecto at compile time), puts ecto/ecto_sql as a non-optional dep or optional dep that consumers must add, and ships a convenience module like Oban.Migrations.up() that users call from their own migration. (4) recommend: add {:ecto, '~> 3.10', optional: true} and {:ecto_sql, '~> 3.10', optional: true} to mix.exs, wrap schema/migration modules in if Code.ensure_loaded?(Ecto.Schema) do ... end, test with mix compile --no-optional-deps.
